One subscription that does it all.
Personalized AI and premium business versions of Gmail, Google Docs, Drive, and more.
Try it free for 14 days at goo.gle/workspace with Gemini.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
The Vatican says doctors at a hospital in Rome have removed a cancerous growth from
Pope Leo's right lung.
As Megan Williams reports, the nodule was detected at an early stage,
and the procedure was described as successful.
The Vatican says tests confirmed the 71-year-old Pope has lung adenocarcinoma,
the most common form of lung cancer.
Surgeons at Rome's Gemini Lee Hospital removed the lower lobe of his right lung
in what his lead surgeon described as an attempt to make the procedure curative.
The minimally invasive operation lasted about 90 minutes,
and the Vatican says there were no complications.
Leo woke normally from the anesthetic and is resting in his hospital room.
The cancer was discovered after a recent routine health check found a small growth on his lung.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
At least six deaths are now reported along Mexico's Pacific Coast
from Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel.
With the November midterm elections now less than three weeks away,
President Trump will be taking part in more campaign rallies for Republican candidates today.
The president is scheduled to be in Montana and Arizona.
Yesterday, the president was in Alaska to rally support for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
NPR's Tamara Keith says Trump's appearances in red states
are being looked at positively by Democratic campaigns.
This is a midterm year with an unpopular president,
and Republicans are playing defense in a whole lot of places that
would have been considered safe seats even just a few months ago.
Does that mean that Democrats are going to win all of these races?
Probably not.
But if Republicans are spending money on defense,
they aren't spending money on offense, and the triage has really started to begin now.
That's NPR's Tamara Keith reporting.
Federal regulators are fining Bank of America more than a billion dollars
for failing to prevent money laundering by its customers.
NPR's Scott Horsley says it marks one of the largest penalties on record by the Treasury Department.
Banks are required to track and report financial transactions they suspect
may be tied to illegal activity.
The Treasury Department says B of A willfully ignored that requirement
and allowed more than $5 billion worth of money to change hands without proper reporting
over a seven-year period stretching back to 2018.
Some of the suspicious moves showed signs of Chinese money laundering networks.
Others had apparent ties to the southwest border.
The bank also agreed to pay more than $11 million to settle apparent sanctions violations
involving Iran, Russia, and other targets.
The bank says in a statement it's committed billions of dollars and thousands of employees
to improving its financial compliance.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Wall Street futures are higher this morning.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Sales of existing homes in the U.S. rose one and a half percent in September,
but the National Association of Realtors says sales were down compared to the same month one year ago.
NPR's Steven Bassaha says higher mortgage rates are keeping many potential homebuyers on the sidelines.
The only months slower for home sales in September was August after making adjustments for seasons.
The National Association of Realtors says this is not a supply issue.
Homes available for sale are at their pre-COVID levels.
Instead, it's about high mortgage rates.
In September, the average for the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose past 6.8 percent.
Since September, rates have only climbed.
Last week, mortgage rates reached a near three-year high of 7.4 percent.
It could go even higher if the Federal Reserve hikes its benchmark interest rate again in the coming months.
Steven Bassaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
Freddie Mac says the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is averaging 7.4 percent.
Major League Baseball's American League Championship Series is now tied at a game apiece
between the Cleveland Guardians and the Tampa Bay Rays.
Last night in Florida, the Rays beat Cleveland 3-1 to even the best of seven series.
Game three is tomorrow night.
Game three of the National League Championship Series is tonight in Los Angeles,
between the Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee leads that series two games to none.
The Dodgers have won the last two World Series.
The winners of each of these series will advance to this year's Fall Classic.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
